uncertainty_targeted: Whether the qualified short-horizon momentum edge (lookback 3/5/10) survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected 10-asset real-data universe.
uncertainty_reduced: Partially: the predeclared cost grid was evaluated and independently reproduced, and the uncertainty about the cost model itself was resolved — the engine's slippage is not a round-trip cost (fixed slippage cancels; proportional slippage scales P&L; fold metrics use within-test equity). The residual uncertainty is the edge's robustness to a genuine external cost, which remains UNVERIFIED until the engine is repaired and the check rerun.
research_result: UNVERIFIED (external cost robustness). Under the existing cost model the qualified momentum edge is cost-robust on the predeclared grid: 6/6 baseline COST_ROBUST assets (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA) survive the realistic, conservative and stress levels, and median cost drag is 0.0000 (range -0.003..+0.001). But the model does not charge a genuine transaction cost: the engine applies the same additive fill price on entry and exit, so fixed slippage cancels over a completed round trip, proportional slippage scales P&L by (1+p), and fold total_return uses only within-test equity change. The AMZN full-sample diagnostic is decisive: zero +5.5373, commission-only +5.5162, slippage-only-stress +5.5460 (higher than zero), full-stress +5.5250; commission (~$21,055 over 4451 fills) is the only real cost. The result is reproducible and independently verified (5 gates MATCH, 171/171 tests), but it does not establish robustness to external transaction costs.
